chunks.arabic_text: سَالِمُ بْنُ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، الْكَنْدِيُّ، السِّجِسْتَانِيُّ. رَوَى عَنْهُ ابْنُهُ مُحَمَّدٌ، لَا يُعْرَفُ، وَرَوَى عَنْهُ غَيْرُهُ. وَهُوَ ضَعِيفٌ، وَرِوَايَتُهُ مُخْتَلِطَةٌ.

translations.en: Sālim b. Abī Salama, al-Kindī, al-Sijistānī. His son Muḥammad narrated from him, he is not recognized, and other (people) than him narrated from him. He is weak, and his narrations are confused.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* classifies Sālim b. Abī Salama al-Kindī al-Sijistānī as a weak (*da‘īf*) narrator with mixed (*mukhtaṭ) narrations, indicating inconsistencies in his memory or transmission. His status is significant in Shia hadith criticism for evaluating the reliability of chains leading to Imami traditions, particularly given his connection to the Kinda tribe and Sijistan region.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Sālim b. Abī Salama al-Kindī in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.لَا يُعْرَفُ: He is not recognized (referring to the son's lack of fame or detailed biographical data)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term for a narrator whose reliability is questionable)
key_terms.مُخْتَلِطَةٌ: Confused/Mixed (referring to narrations that may contain errors or inconsistencies due to the narrator's state)
